name: 74HC00 Quad NAND Gate
summary: Four 2-input NAND gates, the cheapest way to build any logic function at all.
notes: NAND is functionally complete: tie both inputs together for an inverter, NAND two NANDs for AND, invert both inputs for OR. Four gates on one chip covers most glue logic.
Unused inputs must be tied high or low. Floating CMOS inputs oscillate, draw supply current and couple noise into the gates you are using.
The pin order runs gate 1 and 2 down the left (inputs then output), gates 3 and 4 up the right with the output FIRST. Wiring the right-hand gates by analogy with the left is the usual mistake.
HC needs an input within about 1 V of its own rail. Driving a 5 V 74HC00 from 3.3 V logic is out of spec; use 74HCT00, which has TTL thresholds.
Propagation delay is roughly 9 ns at 5 V. For anything slower, the cheaper 74LS00 still exists but draws far more current.
100 nF across pins 7 and 14, at the chip. Four gates switching together pull a current spike the supply trace will not like.

pins.name: 3Y
pins.note: Output comes first on this side, unlike gates 1 and 2.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: 100 nF to GND at the pin.

circuit.title: Set-reset latch

parts.why: Gate 1 output into gate 2 input. The cross-coupling is what gives the pair memory.
Gate 2 output back into gate 1. Now each gate holds the other.
Set input, active low. Pull it down to set, and the pull-up keeps it idle high.
Reset input, active low. Taking both inputs low at once is the state the latch has no answer for.

circuit.note: Two NAND gates and two resistors debounce a changeover switch perfectly, with no timing constant to tune. It is the oldest trick in the book and still the right one for a SPDT button.
